title: GPU compatibility sweep — lab notes and Terraform module uplift plan
body:
Purpose:
This is a working lab notebook for an exhaustive compatibility sweep across Kubernetes node OS/kernel, NVIDIA driver, CUDA, and NCCL permutations we observed in customer private deployments. The goal: produce a conservative upgrade matrix and a Terraform module change list that reduces regression risk for on-prem / VPC deployments (esp. mixed-vendor GPU racks).

Context / motivation:
- Recent customer reports of intermittent OOMs and collectives stalling after CUDA 12.x + driver 535.X upgrades on heterogenous nodes.
- We run a small lab fleet (rack-2) to reproduce and establish a validated support matrix; results feed Redwood Private upgrade playbook and terraform module defaults.
- This doc is intentionally informal — notes-to-self, commands, quick failure traces, and next actions.

Summary findings (high-level):
- Driver 535.x + CUDA 12.1 + NCCL 2.18 is stable on Ubuntu-22.04 with kernel 5.15 for single-GPU workloads but shows collective timeouts on multi-node allreduce with mixed A100/RTX A6000 nodes unless ulimit and GPUDirect settings are adjusted.
- Driver 530.x + CUDA 11.8 + NCCL 2.16 has the widest compatibility with older kernels (5.10 and 5.15), and is our conservative default when customers cannot schedule uniform upgrades.
- Ubuntu-20.04 with older kernels (5.4) frequently requires backported kernel modules (nvidia-dkms) and has spotty nv-peer-mem/GDRCopy behavior; avoid for new clusters.
- Terraform module change: expose a "gpu_driver_channel" variable (stable|latest|customer_pinned) and a preflight check that validates kernel driver ABI compatibility before applying nodepool updates.

Test matrix (abbreviated):
Format: OS | kernel | GPU hw | driver | CUDA | NCCL | multi-node allreduce result
- ubuntu-22.04 | 5.15 | A100 80GB | 535.86 | 12.1 | 2.18 | PASS (single-node), FAIL (multi-node stalls at step 7)
- ubuntu-22.04 | 5.15 | A100 80GB | 530.41 | 11.8 | 2.16 | PASS (single, multi-node)
- ubuntu-20.04 | 5.4  | RTX A6000 | 470.161 | 11.4 | 2.11 | PASS (single), FAIL (GDRCopy retries)
- ubuntu-22.04 | 6.1  | A100 + A40 mixed | 535.86 | 12.1 | 2.18 | FAIL (collectives hang unless NVLink forced off)
- rocky-8      | 4.18 | A100 | 510.60 | 11.7 | 2.14 | PASS (single), WARN (kernel module rebuild required on drift)

Quick repro notes (commands run in lab):
- kubectl run --rm -it nccl-test --image=redwood/nccl-perf:2026-02 --command -- /bin/bash
- run baseline allreduce: python3 /opt/nccl/tests/allreduce.py --world-size 4 --backend nccl
- capture dmesg and driver logs on stall: journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver.service --no-pager | tail -n 200; dmesg | grep -i nvrm
- check GPU affinity & topology: nvidia-smi topo -m; gpustat -c
- when multi-node hang observed, toggling the following helped in some cases:
  - set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^docker0,lo
  - export NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP
  - disable GPUDirect RDMA temporarily: echo 0 > /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/enable_peer_memory (note: requires reboot to revert in lab)

Observed gotchas / notes-to-self (non-exhaustive):
- Mismatched dkms vs non-dkms drivers cause kernel module ABI errors after kernel upgrades; ensure terraform nodepool rolling upgrade sequence rebuilds dkms modules before rebooting.
- Vendor kernel tuning (Mellanox OFED) interacts badly with NCCL 2.18 default ring algorithms; set NCCL_ALGO=RING as a mitigation for heterogeneous NICs.
- Some OEM images ship with an older stashed driver in initramfs; our terraform image build step must zero out /usr/src/nvidia-* before driver install to avoid conflicts.
- SELinux enforcing in RHEL/ROCKY clusters blocked unix socket creation for nccl-tests under /var/run — add a semanage policy in terraform module (policy toggle for customers who need it).

Terraform module uplift notes (proposal):
1) Add variable: gpu_driver_channel (string): stable|latest|pinned. Default: stable. Rationale: avoid auto-picking bleeding-edge driver during nodepool refresh.
2) Preflight validation step (external data source / local-exec): check current kernel version and run nvidia-modprobe --version equivalent in a transient instance to validate ABI compatibility. If mismatch, fail plan with explicit guidance.
3) Rolling update sequence change: drain -> cordon -> install-driver (if needed with DKMS rebuild) -> validate-nvml -> reboot -> run nccl smoke (pod) -> uncordon. Add retries and backoff.
4) Expose node annotation: redwood/gpu-driver-installed: "535.86" for inventory & audit.
5) Example HCL snippet to add to module (rough):
   variable "gpu_driver_channel" { default = "stable" }
   resource "null_resource" "preflight_driver_check" { provisioner "local-exec" {
      command = "python3 scripts/driver_preflight.py ${self.triggers.kernel}"
   }}

Upgrade plan (conservative path for customers with mixed hardware):
- Phase 0: Inventory (2 weeks) — run agent to collect kernel, driver, CUDA, NIC driver versions; classify nodes into homogeneous groups.
- Phase 1: Pilot (1 week) — pick one homogeneous group (A100-only) and run driver upgrade to 530.x (or 535.x if uniform), run full nccl perf suite.
- Phase 2: Gradual rollout (2–4 weeks) — nodepool by nodepool, use terraform module forced sequence; after each nodepool upgrade run smoke (nccl + mkldnn quick tests).
- Phase 3: Post-upgrade validation (1 week) — run longitudinal jobs, monitor for GPU memory leaks and collectives errors.

Rollback plan (fast fallback):
- Preserve previous driver bundle in /opt/redwood/driver-previous/ on each node during upgrade step. If failure observed, use cordon -> install previous driver -> reboot -> run smoke -> uncordon. This is slower but lower blast radius than rolling back entire nodepool.

Lab test results (key logs & snippets):
- dmesg excerpt when multi-node hang (lab node r2-03):
  "[ 4701.633] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 31, pid=21432, Ch 00000002, PID 21432: GpGpu code exception..."
- NCCL debug log: repeated "transport: unable to connect" between IPs 10.10.32.x and 10.10.33.x — found misconfiguration in CNI MTU (1480 vs 1450).
- Terraform plan fail example: dkms module rebuild error seen when kernel version string mismatch; workaround script added to module/scripts/fix-dkms.sh in GH-PR-8123.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- We need a reliable automated allreduce test that scales to 8 nodes without flakiness due to network jitter — can Solutions Eng help adapt our existing perf harness? (ask Samir)
- Should we default terraform gpu_driver_channel to 530.x stable rather than 535 given our multi-node regressions? Need product/PM input.
- How do we record and expose in Console which driver/CUDA were used for a given job/trace (observability tie-in)?

Action items (next short-term steps):
- Priya: land driver_preflight.py that returns non-zero if ABI mismatch (due by 2026-03-10)
- Samir: coordinate Solutions Eng on scaling nccl harness to 8 nodes (due 2026-03-12)
- Ava: prototype terraform variable gpu_driver_channel and preflight null_resource (open PR, GH-PR-8123)
- Ethan: add node annotation prototype and ensure Console ingestion for node inventory (track in JIRA-PI-2473)

Appendix: useful commands / scripts
- driver inventory (run on all nodes via ssh):
  for n in $(cat nodes.txt); do ssh $n "uname -r && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv" >> inventory.csv; done
- quick nccl smoke pod (k8s manifest):
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Pod
  metadata:
    name: nccl-smoke
  spec:
    containers:
    - name: test
      image: redwood/nccl-perf:2026-02
      command: ["/bin/bash","-c","python3 /opt/nccl/tests/allreduce.py --world-size 1 --backend nccl"]
    restartPolicy: Never

References / past artifacts:
- GH-PR-8123 (terraform module scripts + preflight prototype)
- JIRA-PI-2473 (customer incident thread)
- confluence://private-deployments/gpu-compat-sweep (long form matrix)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc light; push polished compatibility matrix to confluence once we have final binary/test matrix. For now, record anomalies and exact commands that reproduced the issues.

-- end of lab notes (Priya)
